script: stop 1 card 2, answer 1: copies a Prep line word for word

findings.problem: Both Scripture quotations omit punctuation or stop early without an ellipsis. Preserve the period after “free” and mark the cutoff after “then” (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture: “Where it cuts off or skips words, it shows "…"”).
The explanation reads like a generic devotional about gifts, performance, and effort. This lighter moment could carry Papa Dorin’s warm, distinctive humor instead of four earnest statements.

“Stand firm” cuts off without an ellipsis, and the quotation ending in “slavery” drops the verse’s period. Scripture quotations must preserve BSB punctuation and mark cutoffs (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation begins partway through Galatians 5:1 without an ellipsis and omits the period after “slavery.” Scripture cutoffs and punctuation must be preserved (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation begins partway through Galatians 5:1 without an ellipsis and omits its final period. Mark the omitted words and preserve BSB punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation omits “Take notice:” without an ellipsis and drops the period after “all.” Preserve the BSB wording and punctuation and mark cutoffs (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation starts partway through Galatians 5:2 without an ellipsis and drops the final period. Scripture quotations must mark cutoffs and preserve punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation starts partway through Galatians 5:2 without an ellipsis and drops the final period. Scripture quotations must mark cutoffs and preserve punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The internal ellipsis correctly marks omitted words, but the quotation also omits the verse’s opening without an ellipsis and drops its final period (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation marks its internal omission but not its omitted opening, and it drops the final period. Preserve BSB punctuation and mark every cutoff (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The full-verse quotation drops the period after “grace.” Quoted Scripture must retain its exact BSB punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
“Grace and law-as-ladder don’t share the same throne” mixes a ladder with a throne and uses abstract theological shorthand. It is neither instantly clear nor Papa Dorin’s plain, natural voice.
The full-verse quotation omits the period after “grace.” Preserve exact BSB punctuation inside Scripture quotation marks (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
“It cuts them off from trusting Christ” changes Paul’s statement. Galatians 5:4 says they have been severed from Christ, not merely severed from trusting Him.
The Scripture fragments omit surrounding words without ellipses, and the second fragment drops the period after “grace.” Mark cutoffs and preserve BSB punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation omits “But” without an ellipsis and drops the period after “righteousness.” Scripture cutoffs must be marked and punctuation preserved (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“What He will finish” and “The Spirit keeps that hope alive” add an explanation of Christ’s future work and the Spirit’s specific activity that Galatians 5:5 does not give. The verse says they eagerly await the hope of righteousness by faith through the Spirit.
The quotation omits “But” without an ellipsis and drops the verse’s final period. Preserve the BSB punctuation and mark cutoffs (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“The Spirit, not the law, carries that hope in them” assigns the Spirit a specific action that the verse does not state. Keep the explanation to awaiting the hope of righteousness by faith through the Spirit.
The quotation omits “But” without an ellipsis and drops the period after “righteousness.” Scripture quotations must preserve punctuation and mark omitted openings (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“Effort has its place” introduces an uncited teaching, while faith being “carried by the Spirit” assigns a relationship the verse does not specify. Galatians 5:5 says they await by faith through the Spirit.

The quotation changes “For in Christ Jesus” to “In Christ Jesus” and drops the final period. This is not exact BSB wording and punctuation; use an accurately marked excerpt or a paraphrase (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

The first Scripture fragment omits its opening without an ellipsis and drops the period after “value”; the second drops the period after “love.” Preserve BSB punctuation and mark cutoffs (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“At the center,” “checklist mindset,” and “the real mark” produce a generic sermon-like explanation. The answer needs Papa Dorin’s concrete, conversational personality rather than a sequence of abstract summaries.
The first quotation changes “For in Christ Jesus” to “In Christ Jesus” and drops the period after “value.” Preserve exact BSB wording and punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

The conclusion that life in Christ is “not about which family you’re from” broadens this verse’s contrast into a claim about lineage. Galatians 5:6 specifically contrasts circumcision and uncircumcision with faith expressing itself through love.
“That’s why he’s so serious about it” supplies Paul’s reason for his seriousness. The text identifies the persuasion’s source negatively but does not state this explanation of Paul’s attitude.
The quotation drops the period after “you.” Quoted Scripture must preserve exact BSB punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The full-verse quotation omits the period after “dough.” Preserve exact BSB punctuation inside quotation marks (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
“If nobody deals with it” adds a condition absent from Paul’s image. Explain the spreading influence without presenting this additional condition as the verse’s teaching.
The full-verse quotation drops the period after “dough.” Quoted Scripture must retain exact BSB punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“Bigger picture,” “the influence,” and “how serious a little error can be” make this a flat teaching summary. This concrete dough image offers room for Papa Dorin’s distinctive bakery voice without making Scripture itself the joke.
The full-verse quotation omits the period after “dough.” Preserve exact BSB punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“Left alone, it moves through the whole community” turns the image into a definite prediction about the entire community and adds an unstated condition. Keep the explanation at the level of the spreading influence illustrated by the leaven.
The quotation begins partway through Galatians 5:10 without an ellipsis and drops the final period. Mark cutoffs and preserve BSB punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
“Will come back to the right view” adds a departure-and-return sequence. Paul says he is confident they “will take no other view”; leave that wording’s scope open.
“Nobody gets to lead people astray for free” gives judgment a punchline-like, punitive finish. A card about serious wrongdoing and judgment needs sober care, not a triumphant closing jab.
The quotation omits the preceding sentence without an ellipsis and drops the period after “be.” Scripture quotations must mark cutoffs and preserve punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation begins partway through the verse without an ellipsis and drops its final period. Preserve BSB punctuation and mark cutoffs (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“Paul is not recommending a promotion” makes a joke on a card about serious wrongdoing and judgment. papa-dorin.md#his-personality says, “A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.”
The quotation changes the BSB’s lowercase “if” to “If” and omits “Now, brothers,” without an ellipsis. Use an exact excerpt with its cutoff marked or paraphrase (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
The quotation changes lowercase “if” to “If” and omits the opening “Now, brothers,” without an ellipsis. Scripture quotation wording must remain exact (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

The quotations leave several cutoffs unmarked: the omitted opening before “you,” the stop after “freedom,” and the omitted surrounding words around the later fragments. They also omit the period after “flesh.” Preserve BSB punctuation and mark cutoffs (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

The quotation omits the opening “For” without an ellipsis and drops the period after “flesh.” The closing “serve one another in love” excerpt also omits “Rather,” without an ellipsis (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

The purported full-verse quotation drops the period within the quoted decree and changes its BSB quotation punctuation. Preserve the exact punctuation or quote only the decree accurately (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“What the law was aiming at” explains the law’s purpose, and “flows from faith in Christ” adds a connection not stated in Galatians 5:14. Keep the verse’s claim that the entire law is fulfilled in this decree, or explicitly support the connection to faith with Galatians 5:6.
The full-verse quotation changes the BSB quotation punctuation and omits the period within the decree. Scripture quotations must preserve exact punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“Remembering the Sabbath is important in the law” introduces a Bible claim without its supporting reference. Galatians 5:14 does not mention the Sabbath. papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture says, “Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.”
The full-verse quotation changes the BSB quotation punctuation and drops the period within the decree. Preserve exact BSB punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“Honoring parents is part of God’s law” is a Bible fact without a supporting reference; Galatians 5:14 does not state that command. papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture says, “Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.”

The Galatians 5:15 quotation omits “But” without an ellipsis and drops its final period. The later quotation from Galatians 5:13 also lacks its reference and an ellipsis marking the omitted opening (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

The quotation marks its internal omission but omits the opening “But” without an ellipsis and drops the final period. Preserve BSB punctuation and mark every cutoff (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).

“Consumed by one another” is a partial-verse quotation with no ellipsis marking its omitted beginning, and it drops the verse’s final period. Scripture excerpts must mark cutoffs and preserve punctuation (papa-dorin.md#facts-and-scripture).
